name: Chemical Process Design: Vexal
subtitle: Chemical Process Design Course
shortDescription: Learn process design by building: close a recycle loop, size a reactor, step a column, trace a pinch. Adaptive quizzes and five cited labs. Free core course.
longDescription:
Chemical Process Design: Vexal is a study companion for chemical engineering students working through a plant design course. It follows one question from the first sketch to the final report: is this process worth building, and how would you lay it out?

Pick a path. The syllabus path takes 23 units in teaching order, from flowsheet synthesis and recycle-and-purge balances through reactors, distillation, heat integration, equipment sizing and costing to risk, safety, sustainability, control structure and the design report. The project path starts from an object to make, such as a recycle loop, a splitter, a heat-recovery network or a budget case, and opens the matching lesson at the step where you get stuck. 16 projects with 81 checked steps feed the same progress record as the syllabus path, so you can swap paths whenever you like.

Five labs let you push sliders and watch the equations respond: stepping stages on a McCabe-Thiele diagram, comparing CSTR and PFR volumes on a Levenspiel plot, sliding hot and cold composite curves to find the pinch, tuning a recycle and purge loop, and searching for the reflux that minimises yearly cost. Every lab shows a cited relation, and Plus adds the second-method check.

Practice adapts to you. There are 738 original questions on four levels from Beginner to Research; 543 have numeric answers, each worked out two different ways before it was written in, and 195 are conceptual items for practice. The app remembers what you know, brings back what you are forgetting and points to the lesson behind each miss, with kind and specific feedback. Sessions run 5, 10, 20 or 40 questions, or a length you choose. Ten multi-step design problems and two timed 180-minute paper-style mocks round it out.

What the app covers, in exact numbers: 73 of 73 mapped course points covered with 8 or more questions each. A Coverage screen lists each point with its lesson, questions and cited sources. A separate informational list of NCEES PE Chemical specification points shows 13 of 41 covered, 20 partly and 8 without content; this is not a PE or FE exam product.

Optional, anonymous usage sharing helps us improve the course; it is explained when you first open the app and can be changed any time under Settings, Privacy and data.

Citations open in a wide sheet that you close with a tap. Type size can be set from 50 to 300 percent. No account is needed, everything works offline and your progress stays on your device.

Free: 3 of the 5 labs (recycle and purge loop, McCabe-Thiele stage stepper, Levenspiel reactor), 8 of the 16 projects, 1 of the 2 mock papers, 5 of the 10 design problems and practice levels 1 and 2. One optional monthly subscription, Vexal Plus, adds the other 2 labs (pinch composites, reflux cost valley), the other 8 projects, the second mock paper and mock review, the other 5 design problems, practice levels 3 and 4, and the second-method checks. Lessons, worked solutions and your progress are never locked. One plain monthly price applies, displayed by the store before you confirm. It renews automatically each month until you cancel in your App Store subscription settings. If you cancel, the plan stops at the end of the month you already paid for; you keep Plus until that day and are not charged a part-month adjustment. Apple decides refund requests. Restore purchases is in Settings and on the Vexal Plus screen.

For teaching only: models are simplified and costs are illustrative, so nothing here is guidance for building, running or funding a real plant. No link to any university, standards body or publisher named in the sources.
